subject: zoology_2
question_text: Mention the advantages of 'lactational amenorrhea method'.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.56, VSAQ 116. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Content revision (examiner audit, 2026-09-05): the memory tip now puts the causation the right way round (ovulation is suppressed first, and the absence of periods follows), and the method is named a natural method, which is where NCERT lists it, instead of a hormonal one.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: It prevents conception
steps.why: Breast feeding suppresses ovulation, so no ovum is released to be fertilised.
common_mistakes: Calling it a barrier method. It is a natural method — intense breast feeding suppresses ovulation, and no device or drug is used.
Writing that it works after breast feeding stops. It works only while it continues.
steps.memory_tip: Intense breast feeding suppresses ovulation, so there are no periods and almost no chance of conception.
steps.margin_note: The condition matters: only while breast feeding continues.
lines: As long as the mother breast feeds her
child, the chances of conception are

steps.label: It helps the baby
steps.why: The milk carries the mother's antibodies, so the baby is protected while its own defences develop.
common_mistakes: Leaving out the protection against allergies.
steps.memory_tip: The same method feeds the baby and protects it.
steps.margin_note: One line for the baby's advantage.
lines: Breast fed babies have better immunity

insider_note: Two advantages, one for the mother and one for the baby. Most answers give only the contraceptive one.
